This variance acts as a scalar descriptor of motion activity, computed via \(\sigma^2_{\text{VAM}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} (v_i - \bar{v})^2\). It captures temporal fluctuations in motion magnitude, enabling discrimination between static and dynamic scenes. The VAM_extract tool provides the necessary input by parsing motion vectors from compressed streams, assuming H.264 compliance. The maximally discriminative threshold \(T_{\text{max}}\) is determined via Kullback-Leibler divergence between class distributions, optimizing separation between global and reaction-phase content. Dualities emerge in that VAM variance can be interpreted both as a statistical moment and as a signal-to-noise ratio proxy. Failure modes include corrupted motion vector data, misalignment of motion estimation, and insufficient temporal resolution.
